kinds.title: Households and people
kinds.summary: Nine households of people. A household decides how much of its money to spend each month and which shop gets it. People do not choose jobs one by one: firms hire from the unemployed (cheapest reservation wage first, ties to higher skill). A household's class is a label worked out from what it owns and earns; it is never chosen.
decides: How much to spend on food, goods and services this month
Which firm in each sector gets that spending
Whether to found a firm in the dormant slot (a Worker or Manager household with enough savings)
Capital-owning households: how much to give lobbying
observes: Its savings and last disposable income
Every shop's price and stock
The interest rate, firms' profit and unmet demand (for founding a firm)
kinds.rule: food = min(need x food price, savings); discretionary = min(propensity x max(0, disposable - food need) + wealth spending, savings - food); services = services share x discretionary; goods = the rest. Shop weight = stock x (average price / price) ^ elasticity, where the average price is weighted by stock

params.label: Share of discretionary spending on services
Capitalists and Rentiers: spending out of wealth
params.unit: share of net wealth per month

variants.label: Capitalist
variants.decision: Owns firms or the bank and lives mostly on profit; spends only part of income and funds lobbying.
variants.rule: owns assets and capital share of recent income above the threshold, rent not the main part

variants.label: Rentier
variants.decision: Lives mostly on rent from homes it lets; spends part of income and funds lobbying.
variants.rule: as Capitalist, but rent received is above the rentier share of capital income

variants.label: Manager
variants.decision: Skilled and well paid; spends most of income and is the person who receives lobbying money.
variants.rule: employed, top skill above the skill threshold and pay above the skilled wage ratio times the base wage

variants.label: Worker
variants.decision: Lives on wages; spends nearly all income, buying food first.

variants.label: Dependent
variants.decision: No one in the household has a job; lives on benefits and savings, food first.
variants.rule: no employed member, and not a Capitalist or Rentier

classParams.label: Capital share of income that makes a Capitalist or Rentier
Rent share of capital income that makes a Rentier
Pay needed for a Manager, against the base wage

kinds.title: Firms
kinds.summary: Factory, Farm and Shop, plus one dormant slot a household can start. Each firm decides how many workers it wants, what to pay and what to charge. (Market, Regulated and Coop are not kinds of firm: they are the town-wide economic system the player picks, which changes ownership and payout rules.)
decides: How many workers to want and how many jobs to post (hiring up to a monthly cap)
Whether to let people go: only after a sustained surplus of workers, the least skilled first
The base wage, adjusted each month
The price it charges
How much to invest and borrow
observes: Expected sales: A smoothed average of past demand for what the firm makes.
Inventory: Unsold stock the firm holds.
Inventory cover wanted: How many months of sales the firm likes to hold as stock (services cannot be stored, so they hold none).
Workers: The people the firm employs.
Skilled workers: Workers whose skill is at or above the skilled threshold.
Effective labour per worker: What an average worker contributes after skill and commute time.
Output per unit of labour: What one unit of labour would make now, given the firm's capital, technology, weather and climate.
Workers wanted: The headcount that would produce the output the firm wants.
Months overstaffed: How many months in a row the firm has had more workers than it wants.
Base wage: The firm's base monthly wage.
Minimum wage: The legal wage floor (the player's lever).
Unemployment: The town's smoothed unemployment rate, which firms watch when they set wages.
Sector productivity growth: How fast output per worker grows in the firm's sector; wages follow it so that wages and prices do not drift apart.
Its unit cost (wages plus carbon cost per unit)
kinds.rule: Hiring, firing and the wage have their own rules under Decisions below (generated from the code). Price moves a share of the way to (1 + markup) x unit cost; expected sales = smoothing x demand + (1 - smoothing) x previous

params.label: Share of the inventory gap closed per month
Share of jobs that are skilled
Effective labour assumed for an empty firm
Most people hired in a month
Most people fired in a month
Largest wage change in a month
Expected wage growth on top of productivity
Share of productivity growth passed into wages
Share of the price gap closed per month
Weight of this month's demand in expected sales

kinds.title: Bank
kinds.summary: One bank that lends to firms against its equity, takes deposits and pays a dividend from excess capital. It follows a rule; it does not weigh individual borrowers.
decides: The interest rate each firm pays
How much a firm may borrow (a leverage cap and the bank's capital ratio)
How much of excess capital to pay out
observes: The base rate set by the player
Each firm's debt against its assets (leverage)
Its own equity and loans
kinds.rule: firm loan rate = base rate + base spread + leverage spread x leverage + system spread; leverage = debt / (capital value + cash); borrowing limited to max leverage x assets

params.label: Base spread over the policy rate
Extra spread per unit of leverage
Share of excess capital paid out

kinds.title: Government
kinds.summary: The government collects taxes, pays benefits and spending and borrows for deficits, all at the levels the player sets. Its own rule is legitimacy: a score that drifts with wellbeing, unemployment, inequality and debt.
decides: Nothing on its own about policy: levers are the player's
How much to borrow or repay to keep a cash target
How much of its spending it can actually fund
observes: Wellbeing, smoothed unemployment, the Gini coefficient and debt against GDP
Whether the bank was bailed out this month
kinds.rule: legitimacy change = wellbeing weight x (wellbeing - 0.5) - unemployment weight x max(0, unemployment - threshold) - inequality weight x max(0, Gini - threshold) - debt weight x max(0, debt/GDP - 1) - bailout penalty

kinds.title: Lobbyists
kinds.summary: Not a separate body: Capitalist and Rentier households give a share of their capital income to the wealthiest Manager household, which acts as the lobbyist. Together with union density this erodes the policies the player sets. The player sees the nominal lever and the effective one.
decides: How much each capital-owning household gives (a share of capital income, up to its savings and the campaign cap)
observes: Capital income and savings
GDP, wage share and unemployment (for union strength)
kinds.rule: capital pull = lobby k x spend / monthly GDP, capped at the system's maximum; labour pull = union density x wage share x labour weight; net = clamp(capital - labour, 0, max); effective lever = nominal x (1 - net)

params.label: Influence per unit of spending against GDP
Largest net erosion of a lever

kinds.title: Nature
kinds.summary: Forest and commons are not agents: they follow fixed rules for growth, harvest and decay. The one chance event is an owner fencing off an open commons.
decides: Nothing: it responds to emissions, harvest and fire
observes: Cumulative emissions, forest stock, commons use and access rule
kinds.rule: see the Forest and commons topic for growth and the sink; enclosure is a monthly chance while the commons are open

params.label: Monthly chance of enclosure, Market system

kinds.title: Weather
kinds.summary: Droughts and fires are not decisions. Their odds rise with climate stress, which rises as the carbon budget runs down. They are the main place where the random seed matters.
decides: Nothing: odds follow climate stress, dryness and fire stations
observes: Climate stress, forest tiles, drought severity, fire station coverage
kinds.rule: drought chance = base x (1 + gain x stress); ignition chance = base x (1 + gain x stress) x dryness x standing share x (1 - resilience cut); spread chance = spread base x (1 + drought gain x severity) x (1 - station cut)

params.label: Base spread chance per neighbouring forest tile

kinds.title: The estate and its pilot
kinds.summary: One very rich household that does not work, owns the Farm, a posh house, a private jet and a runway. It is an ordinary household for spending, tax and class (it comes out Capitalist), with two extra rules: the jet flies by chance and pays the carbon price, and the estate pays a pilot, who is a worker in another household.
decides: Whether to pay the pilot in full each month (it pays what it holds, up to the wage)
Whether to let the pilot go after months of short pay, and to rehire once it can afford wages again
observes: Its savings, the carbon price after lobbying, whether the pilot is employed
kinds.rule: each month one random draw decides whether the jet flies (only with an employed pilot); a flight adds its tonnes to emissions and charges carbon price x tonnes; the pilot's wage moves from the estate to the pilot's household; unpaid for the maximum number of months: let go; savings cover the rehire months of wages: hired back

params.label: Chance the jet flies in a month

randomness.probability: drought base x (1 + stress gain x climate stress), clamped to 0 to 1
randomness.when: each month with no drought running and climate stress above zero

randomness.event: How severe and how long a drought is
randomness.probability: two uniform draws on 0..1: severity = min(1, sev_min + u x (span base + span stress x stress)); months = dur_min + floor(u x (span base + span stress x stress))

randomness.event: A fire spreads to a neighbouring forest tile
randomness.probability: spread chance x (1 + drought gain x severity) x (1 - station cut if covered)
randomness.when: each month, once for each standing forest tile next to a burning tile

params.label: Cut inside a fire station's reach

randomness.probability: fire base x (1 + stress gain x stress) x dryness x standing forest share x (1 - resilience cut)
randomness.when: each month with climate stress above zero and some forest standing

randomness.probability: one uniform pick among the standing forest tiles
randomness.when: only when a new fire starts

randomness.event: A home next to a fire is damaged
randomness.probability: a fixed chance per home within one tile of a fire
randomness.when: each month for each such home; the draw happens only when the chance is above zero, and in the shipped content it is zero (off)

randomness.event: An owner fences off an open commons
randomness.probability: the economic system's enclosure chance; the richest Capitalist or Rentier household becomes the owner
randomness.when: each month; the draw is always taken, but it only counts while the commons are open and the chance is above zero (Market only in the shipped content), so the commons rule never shifts the shared stream

randomness.event: A household founds a firm in the dormant slot
randomness.probability: mobility rate x max(0, sector return - base rate), clamped to 0..1
randomness.when: every month the draw is taken (so it never shifts the shared stream); it only counts when a household has the savings and a dormant slot sits in a sector with enough unmet demand

params.label: Unmet demand needed in the sector

randomness.probability: the fixed monthly flight chance; the flight happens only if the pilot is employed (the draw is taken either way, so a dismissal never shifts the shared random stream)
randomness.when: each month while the estate exists

params.label: Chance the jet flies in a month

deterministic: Everything else is deterministic: spending, shop choice, hiring, wages, prices, credit, taxes, lobbying and legitimacy use no random draws.

The seed fixes two streams of random numbers. The weather stream drives droughts and fires only, so nothing the player does can change when or where they strike; the shared stream drives whether a commons is fenced off, whether a household founds a firm and when the estate's jet flies, and each of those draws is taken every month whether or not it counts. Changing the seed changes both; it does not change the starting town.
The starting differences between households (income, savings, skill, who owns what) are written in content/initial_town.json, not drawn.
